question: Which radiographic sign is used to detect pneumoperitoneum on a SUPINE abdominal radiograph when the patient cannot be positioned erect?

answers.text: Air under the right hemidiaphragm on the AP film.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Air under the diaphragm is the classic sign on an ERECT film. On a supine film, free air rises to the anterior abdomen and is not visualised under the diaphragm in the same way.

answers.text: Rigler's sign — visualisation of BOTH sides of the bowel wall when free intraperitoneal gas outlines the outer bowel wall.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Rigler's sign (double wall sign) occurs when free intraperitoneal gas on the outer surface and intraluminal gas on the inner surface both outline the bowel wall — making it visible as a lucent line rather than the usual single mucosal surface. It is the most reliable sign of pneumoperitoneum on a supine film.

answers.text: Doge's cap sign — lucency over the liver.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Partially valid but incomplete. While a subhepatic lucency may be seen, Rigler's sign (double wall sign) is the most specific and widely taught sign of pneumoperitoneum on a supine film.
Incorrect. Loss of the psoas shadow indicates retroperitoneal pathology (haemorrhage, abscess). It is not a sign of free intraperitoneal gas (pneumoperitoneum).

overallFeedback.feedback: Review emergency signs on abdominal films. Rigler's sign (both surfaces of the bowel wall visible) is the sign of pneumoperitoneum on a supine film; free subdiaphragmatic air is the sign on an erect film.
Correct. Rigler's sign — the double wall sign — is the key indicator of pneumoperitoneum on a supine film.
